description: Demonstrates the grouped/sibling ResultSets proposal from Discussion #45 (proposed, not yet finalized) in a third, independent domain: a multi-model comparison, the second motivating use case issue #36 named alongside mutation testing ('a seed-sweep or a multi-model comparison') that had not yet been grounded in a real system. Verified against promptfoo/promptfoo's actual current source (src/types/index.ts): EvaluateResult.provider: {id, label} identifies which model produced a given row, and CompletedPrompt.provider + its .metrics (PromptMetricsSchema: score, testPassCount, testFailCount, ...) is exactly the consumer-computed per-provider rollup this RFC's group design already assumes -- confirming the join-key-on-member/rollup-computed-by-consumer shape a fifth time, independently of W&B, MLflow, Stryker, and Optuna. providers are configured as an ordered array (providers: z.array(ApiProviderSchema) in promptfoo's schema) and evaluated in that order, so group.sequence is well-defined here too, the same way it was for Optuna's grid search -- not just for adaptive/incremental producers that must omit it. The provider ids below (anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6, openai:gpt-4.1, google:gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview) and the suite's premise (grading how accurately each model describes an image) are taken directly from promptfoo's own real, current example built for exactly this purpose: examples/compare-claude-vs-gpt-image/promptfooconfig.yaml. group.role here is the real provider id string rather than mutation testing's 'mutant' or the grid search fixture's 'candidate' -- role is open specifically so each domain can name its own members without a spec change.
